description: Adana Kebab is a celebrated Turkish delight, featuring hand-minced lamb expertly seasoned with fiery red pepper flakes and sumac. These succulent skewers are traditionally grilled over charcoal, offering a smoky flavor and tender texture that's simply irresistible. Perfect for a hearty lunch, it's often served with fresh lavash bread and a vibrant onion salad.

ingredients.notes: mild or hot, depending on preference

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables
instructions.text: Finely mince the red and green bell peppers, red onion, and garlic. The finer the mince, the better the texture of the kebab. You can use a food processor, but be careful not to create a paste; aim for a very fine dice. Squeeze out any excess liquid from the minced vegetables to prevent the kebab mixture from becoming watery.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground lamb with the minced vegetables, red pepper paste, pul biber, ground sumac, salt, and black pepper. Add 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Using your hands, knead the mixture vigorously for at least 5-7 minutes. This kneading is crucial for developing the meat's texture and ensuring all ingredients are well incorporated and the mixture becomes sticky.

instructions.title: Chill the Kebab Mixture
instructions.text: Once thoroughly mixed, cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate the kebab mixture for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 1-2 hours. Chilling helps the meat firm up, making it easier to shape onto skewers and preventing it from falling off during grilling.

instructions.title: Shape the Kebabs
instructions.text: Prepare flat, wide metal skewers (traditional Adana skewers are best). Take a portion of the chilled meat mixture (about 150-200g per kebab). Wet your hands slightly with water or olive oil, then firmly press and spread the meat evenly along the skewer, ensuring it's about 1.5-2 cm thick. Pinch the meat along the skewer at intervals to create the characteristic Adana kebab indentations.

instructions.title: Grill the Kebabs
instructions.text: Preheat your grill (charcoal is traditional, but a gas grill or broiler works) to medium-high heat. Brush the kebabs lightly with the remaining olive oil. Place the skewers on the hot grill, turning them frequently to ensure even cooking and a beautiful char on all sides. Cook for about 12-18 minutes, depending on thickness and desired doneness. The internal temperature should reach 71C (160F).

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Carefully remove the cooked kebabs from the grill. Serve hot with fresh lavash or pita bread, sliced red onion salad (with sumac and parsley), grilled tomatoes and peppers, and a squeeze of lemon. Adana Kebab is best enjoyed fresh off the grill.

tips: For the most authentic texture, ensure your lamb is minced very finely or hand-chopped. The fat content is important for juiciness, so avoid overly lean lamb.
The kneading step is critical; it helps bind the meat proteins, preventing the kebab from falling apart on the skewer. Don't skip or shorten this process.
Serve Adana Kebab immediately after grilling. Pair it with a simple Shepherd's Salad (Çoban Salata) and a refreshing glass of Ayran for a complete Turkish experience.
article:
Adana Kebab, a culinary jewel from the vibrant city of Adana in Turkey, is more than just a meal; it's an experience. Known for its fiery spice, succulent texture, and unique preparation, it has captivated taste buds worldwide. While often enjoyed as a hearty dinner, it also makes for an incredibly satisfying and flavorful Turkish lunch. Imagine biting into perfectly grilled, hand-minced lamb, seasoned with a symphony of spices, served fresh off the skewer. If you're looking to bring the authentic flavors of Turkey into your kitchen, mastering the Adana Kebab recipe is a fantastic place to start. This article will guide you through every step to create this iconic dish, transforming your midday meal into an exotic escape.

## What is Adana Kebab?
Adana Kebab is a long, hand-minced meat kebab mounted on a wide iron skewer and grilled over an open charcoal fire. Originating from Adana, Turkey, it holds a geographical indication, requiring adherence to specific standards. Traditionally made from male lamb, specifically from the leg and tail fat, and minced with a large, sharp 'zırh' knife, this meticulous hand-mincing is crucial for its characteristic texture. The meat is mixed with red capia pepper, fresh red chili flakes, and salt, with minimal other spices or herbs traditionally added. The fat content is vital for moisture and flavor. While the traditional Adana Kebab recipe requires specific tools, home cooks can achieve a delicious rendition with standard equipment, offering a perfect balance of spice, fat, and smoky char.

## Ingredients You Need for Adana Kebab
Crafting an authentic-tasting Adana Kebab at home requires quality, fresh ingredients. The magic lies in simplicity and balance.

*   **For the Kebab Meat:**
    *   1 kg (about 2.2 lbs) ground lamb (preferably 80/20 fat content)
    *   1-2 large red bell peppers (capia peppers if available), finely minced or grated
    *   2-3 fresh red chilies (e.g., Fresno or long red peppers), finely minced (adjust to your spice preference)
    *   1-2 teaspoons Turkish red pepper flakes (pul biber or Maras pepper), or regular red pepper flakes
    *   1 teaspoon black pepper (freshly ground)
    *   1.5-2 teaspoons salt (or to taste)
